name: neoplasia overview
title: Neoplasia decision chart: a mass is pre-malignant while the basement membrane is intact (dysplasia, carcinoma in situ) and malignant once through it, then staged by how it spread (direct T, lymphatic N, hematogenous M) and graded by differentiation; each column gives what defines it, how it is found and what it means

root.title: A MASS: is it a neoplasm, is it MALIGNANT, and how far has it SPREAD?
lines: describe it first: size, shape, surface/borders, colour, consistency
a mass is NOT always cancer: it may be a cyst, abscess, blood or fluid

groups.title: THROUGH the basement membrane: MALIGNANT
lines: SPREAD is the one criterion · stage it by HOW it spread: tumour, node, metastasis (TNM)
GRADE it by how the cells look: well differentiated (I, slower) → poorly or UNDIFFERENTIATED (immunohistochemistry to find the origin)

head: h
Dysplasia
mild → severe
mean: Can turn into cancer over time

head: h
Carcinoma in situ
= HIGH-GRADE dysplasia · stage Tis
def: pushes on an INTACT basement membrane
find: but has NOT invaded normal tissue

head: h
Direct spread: T
invades ADJACENT structures
mean: T only, N0 M0 → STAGE I

head: h
Lymphatic spread: N
into lymph vessels + nodes
find: e.g. lung cancer in the nodes
• ↓ breath sounds; feel the SUPRACLAVICULAR fossa
mean: LOTS of nodes can mean STAGE IV

head: h
Hematogenous spread: M
through the blood, body-wide
find: via the veins, through the liver
